title: Perf baseline & representative workload suite — Kickoff notes (2026-01-06)
content:
Doc: Working notes (not the Confluence source-of-truth). Please don’t forward externally.

Meeting: Perf baseline & representative workload suite (Q1 2026)
Date/time: 2026-01-06 10:00–11:30 PT
Facilitator: Talia Benson

Why we’re here (Mateo):
- We keep arguing about “is this faster?” with no stable reference.
- Need locked, reproducible Q1 baselines for top-served models + a representative workload suite.
- Baselines become the reference for:
  1) runtime release qualification
  2) perf regression detection/gating
  3) model catalog perf profiles
  4) limited customer-facing transparency (where approved)

Non-goals (explicit):
- Not a “who has the best p99 in the world” marketing benchmark.
- Not collecting raw customer prompts.
- Not solving all fleet heterogeneity in Q1; we’ll define what we can normalize vs what we hold constant.

Attendees
Runtime:
- Mateo Alvarez (exec sponsor)
- Noah Patel (perf architect)
- Hiro Tanaka (kernel perf lead)
- Sofia Ivanova (scheduling/batching lead)
- Marcus Reed (perf suite maintainer)
- Rina Kobayashi (benchmark harness owner)

Applied ML perf/evals:
- Jonas Weber (methodology)
- Sana Farid (stats/variance budgets)

SRE/Obs/Telemetry/Release:
- Sean Gallagher (SRE)
- Logan Wright (telemetry)
- Connor O’Brien (release qualification)
- Sahana Iyer (CI/nightly automation)

Product:
- Henry Cho (customer-facing perf transparency)
- Paula Mendes (publish/approval policy)

Agenda
1. Define “baseline” philosophy (Noah)
2. Draft model list + hardware/region matrix (Arjun not present; Noah to follow up)
3. Traffic shapes / workload suite draft (Claire not present; Jonas to seed)
4. Methodology + variance budget outline (Sana)
5. Tooling & rollout (Rina/Sahana/Connor/Sean)
6. Open questions + action items

Notes

1) Baseline philosophy (Noah)
- We need two levels:
  A) Macro baseline: end-to-end (client->gateway->runtime->first token + streaming cadence + completion) on representative shapes.
  B) Micro baseline: kernel/scheduler sensitive microbench (prefill/decode token throughput, attention kernels by seq len, KV cache ops) for PR-level signal.
- Baselines must be reproducible by rerun (same suite, same configs, pinned env) and interpretable (scheduler + kernel metrics to explain tails).
- We should version baseline artifacts like a release: suite version + runtime SHA + driver/CUDA + compiler flags + instance type + region + seeds.

2) Initial model list (draft, to be finalized week 1–2)
Goal: cover “what we actually serve” + a couple of stressors (long context, streaming heavy).

Draft “must include” (Noah’s proposal):
- Chat general-purpose (mid-size):
  - Llama 3.1 8B Instruct (or current Redwood default equivalent)
- Chat large/high quality:
  - Llama 3.1 70B Instruct (or current Redwood default equivalent)
- Long-context:
  - Llama 3.1 8B/70B with 128k context config (if supported), or alternative long-context SKU we actually ship
- Embeddings:
  - one top embedding model (to be confirmed with Product + catalog)
- Reranker (optional but likely):
  - one reranking model used in hosted API

Notes:
- Hiro: kernel behavior differs materially across model families (GQA vs MHA, rope scaling, etc). We should avoid “too many models”, but enough to not overfit.
- Jonas: If we publish anything externally, it must align with model catalog naming + pinned versions.
- Henry/Paula: external sharing requires explicit policy + approvals; internal baselines can include more detail.

Model versioning questions:
- Do we baseline “model X @ quant profile Y” as separate entries? (likely yes)
- Which quantization profiles matter for production? (INT8? FP8? depends by hardware)
- How to handle “fast path” kernels that differ per GPU SKU? (separate baseline per hardware class)

3) Hardware / region matrix (rough)
We need to be careful on scope explosion.

Proposed minimum (Sean + Vanessa follow-up needed):
- Hardware SKUs: 2 primary GPU types used in hosted + dedicated (e.g., H100-class, L40S/A10-class) — names to confirm.
- Regions: 2 regions for baseline (one “primary”, one “secondary”) to catch region-level differences.

SRE concerns:
- Fleet mix in a region can drift (driver/CUDA mismatch, minor silicon bins). We need enforcement or at least detection.
- Suggest dedicated “benchmark pools” (tainted nodes) for baseline jobs.

4) Traffic shapes / workload suite (first draft)
We need canonical shapes that map to customer patterns. We’ll maintain a taxonomy and use it across teams.

Key dimensions to cover:
- Prompt length distribution (short, medium, long, heavy-tail)
- Output length distribution (short completion vs long generation)
- Streaming vs non-streaming
- Concurrency regime (steady state vs bursty, ramp-up, mixed tenants)
- Cache conditions (warm vs cold; prefix cache hit rates; KV cache eviction pressure)

Draft “shape shortlist” (names are placeholders):
1) CHAT-SHORT-STREAM
- prompt: 200–800 tokens
- output: 50–250 tokens
- streaming: yes
- concurrency: moderate steady (e.g., 16–64)
- cache: mixed (some prefix repeats)

2) CHAT-MIXED-NONSTREAM
- prompt: mixture (p50 ~1k, p95 ~4k)
- output: 200–800 tokens
- streaming: no
- concurrency: steady high
- cache: mostly cold

3) LONGCTX-STREAM
- prompt: 8k–32k tokens (with long tail; maybe include 64k+ if we support)
- output: 200–1k tokens
- streaming: yes
- concurrency: low-to-moderate (tail latency sensitive)
- cache: cold + KV pressure scenario

4) BURSTY-CONCURRENCY-CHAT
- prompt: short/medium
- output: short/medium
- streaming: mixed (50/50)
- concurrency: bursts (spike 10x over 30–60s), then decay
- focus: scheduler/backpressure/load shedding behavior

5) MULTITENANT-MIX
- two “tenants” with different shapes (e.g., Tenant A short streaming, Tenant B long non-stream)
- focus: fairness + tail isolation + batch composition

6) CACHE-WARMUP-SCENARIO
- a run stage that intentionally warms prefix cache for a subset of prompts, then measures a window
- focus: how cache hit rate affects TTFT/TPOT and throughput; ensures we measure both warm and cold.

Jonas notes:
- “Representative” means: derived from aggregated stats (prompt length histograms, output length histograms, streaming fraction, concurrency traces), not raw content.
- We need a documented mapping: which shape corresponds to which common app category.

Open question: how to define/construct prompt text for synthetic workloads
- use public domain / canned prompts + randomization to avoid memorization and caching artifacts
- avoid prompts that trigger safety filters / tool calling unpredictably
- stable tokenization is critical; lock tokenizer + prompt set version

5) Metric definitions (TTFT/TPOT/etc.) + streaming specifics
Logan + Jonas: we need crisp definitions.

Proposed primary metrics (macro):
- TTFT (time to first token)
- TPOT (time per output token) OR tokens/sec during decode
- End-to-end latency for non-streaming (request->full response)
- Throughput (tokens/sec per GPU and per replica; also req/s)
- Error rate (5xx, timeouts, cancellations)
- Tail stats: p50/p95/p99 (and maybe p99.9 for internal only)

Streaming TTFT definition debate (flagged for follow-up):
- Server-side TTFT: from request accepted by gateway/runtime to first token produced (timestamp inside runtime)
- Client-observed TTFT: from client send to first byte/chunk received

Current leaning:
- Use server-side TTFT as baseline primary (less noisy, comparable across regions).
- Also record client-observed TTFT in harness as a secondary for sanity / “what customers feel”.
- Must document clock sources and what is included (queue wait, batching wait, network).

Instrumentation gaps noted:
- Need queue wait time distributions in runtime (prefill queue vs decode queue)
- Batch composition counters (how many requests in batch, average prompt length per batch)
- Backpressure/load-shed events
- KV cache hit annotations per request (or aggregated per run stage)

6) Variance budgets & run structure (Sana)
- We should set a target variance budget per metric so we can distinguish noise vs real regression.
- For each shape+model+hardware+region cell, define:
  - warmup period
  - measurement window
  - number of trials
  - acceptable run-to-run deltas

Early proposal:
- TTFT p95: within +/- 5% run-to-run under pinned env
- TPOT p95: within +/- 3% (decode is usually more stable)
- p99 metrics may require more samples; define minimum N and possibly use confidence intervals.

Sean: For gating, we need:
- a “warn-only” phase with dashboards + human review
- then soft fail (needs override)
- then hard fail in CI/nightly when stable

7) Tooling plan (Rina / Sahana / Marcus)
- Benchmark harness should output a standardized JSON schema including:
  - suite version + workload id
  - model id + quant profile
  - hardware + driver/CUDA + runtime build
  - region + cluster id + node pool id
  - metrics summary (p50/p95/p99)
  - raw histograms if affordable (maybe sampling)
  - linkable artifact bundle (configs, prompt set version, seeds)

Where will it run?
- Nightly: perf-canary pipeline (Sahana)
- On-demand: engineer can run “baseline cell” locally against a benchmark pool

Dashboard requirements (not decided, but noted):
- slicers: model / region / hardware / traffic shape / suite version / runtime SHA
- drilldown: from macro regression -> scheduler metrics -> kernel microbench

8) Publishing / customer-facing constraints (Henry / Paula)
- Internal: full detail ok (including per-region, per-hardware).
- External (if any): likely aggregated, curated, and only after approval workflow.
- Need policy for what can be shared and how we attest to methodology.

Open questions (parking lot)
1) What is the “top-served models” list as of Q1? Who owns final call? (Product + Runtime + Catalog)
2) How many regions/hardware SKUs are minimum viable without exploding matrix size?
3) Streaming TTFT: server vs client vs both — which is baseline primary? (tentative: server primary, client secondary)
4) How do we handle kernel autotuning nondeterminism? Do we pin autotune cache / seeds / kernel selection?
5) Do we run baselines on hosted-only stacks or include dedicated/private configs? (likely hosted first; dedicated next)
6) How do we represent mixed-tenant fairness? One run with two workloads interleaved? Separate tenant lanes?
7) What is the right “cache warm” definition? Prefix cache vs KV cache; measure hit rate how?
8) Storage/retention: how long do we keep raw run artifacts? (cost + privacy)
9) Can we safely use aggregated production histograms without creating “customer-derived confidential info” risk? (needs guidance)

Decisions / alignment achieved today
- We will build a versioned workload suite with named traffic shapes.
- Baseline artifacts must be reproducible (pinned env, seeds, prompt sets, runtime build metadata).
- Baselines will be used for release qualification; rollout gates will be phased (warn-only -> blocking).
- We will measure both macro (E2E) and micro (kernel/scheduler targeted) signals.

Action items
(Owners listed; dates are targets and will shift once tickets are created/linked.)

Program / docs
- [Talia] Create initiative + sub-tickets in Linear and link notes (ENG-4821 etc.) — by 2026-01-07
- [Noah + Jonas] Draft “baseline philosophy + metric definitions” (TTFT/TPOT, streaming) for Confluence — by 2026-01-13

Models / matrix
- [Noah] Pull top-served model list + current catalog versions; propose final model set v0 — by 2026-01-10
- [Arjun] (follow-up offline) Propose hardware/region matrix + priorities; include quant profiles — by 2026-01-14
- [Henry + Paula] Confirm which model names/versions are allowed for any external-facing references — by 2026-01-20

Workload suite
- [Jonas + Sana] Define initial traffic-shape taxonomy v0 (names, parameter ranges, rationale, mapping to apps) — by 2026-01-17
- [Rina + Marcus] Propose harness schema + artifact packaging (configs, seeds, prompt set versioning) — by 2026-01-24

Runtime instrumentation
- [Sofia + Julian] List required scheduler metrics (queue wait, batch composition, backpressure) and gaps vs current telemetry — by 2026-01-17
- [Logan + Nadia] Validate TTFT instrumentation for streaming (first chunk timestamp edge cases) and propose fixes — by 2026-01-24

SRE / variance / gating
- [Sean + Sana] Draft variance study plan: number of trials, confidence intervals, variance budget per metric — by 2026-01-24
- [Sahana + Connor] Draft perf gate rollout plan for release train (warn-only -> soft fail -> hard fail) — by 2026-01-31
- [Sean + Vanessa] Propose benchmark pool strategy to reduce fleet/env drift; define enforcement/detection — by 2026-01-31

Risks called out (summary)
- Fleet variance (driver/CUDA mismatches) will swamp p99 without pinned pools.
- Kernel autotuning nondeterminism can create false regressions.
- Cache behavior is tricky; must define warm/cold precisely.
- Metrics cardinality/cost (dashboards + logs) if we slice too much.
- Confidentiality: any production-derived shapes must be aggregated/sanitized.

Next meeting
- 2026-01-13: review model list v0 + traffic-shape taxonomy v0 + confirm definitions.

Notes to self (Talia)
- Make sure Confluence pages are set up early so Drive notes don’t become the de facto spec.
- Confirm ownership: Marcus as long-term maintainer for suite + dashboards coordination?
- Ask Product for the “top-served” list + any upcoming catalog migrations (avoid baselining a model that’s being deprecated).
